_meta.indication: Treatment of patients with neovascular (wet) age-related macular degeneration

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multi-center, double-blind, double-masked, sham-controlled (superiority) study; subjects received sham, ranibizumab 0.3mg, or ranibizumab 0.5mg monthly for 24 months in a 1:1:1 ratio
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects with angiographically determined, minimally classic or occult subfoveal neovascular AMD
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects who lost fewer than 15 letters (approximately 3 lines) in the BCVA score at Month 12 compared to baseline
pivotal_trials.result: At Month 12, loss of <15 letters: 95% LUCENTIS 0.5 mg vs 62% sham (difference 32%, 95% CI 26%, 39%); gain of >=15 letters 34% vs 5% (difference 29%); mean change +7.2 vs -10.5 letters; p<0.01

nct_ctgov.title: A Study to Evaluate rhuFab V2 in Subjects With Minimally Classic or Occult Subfoveal Neovascular Macular Degeneration

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multi-center, double-blind, double-masked, active-controlled (non-inferiority) study; subjects received verteporfin PDT, ranibizumab 0.3mg, or ranibizumab 0.5mg monthly for 24 months in a 1:1:1 ratio
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects with angiographically determined, predominantly classic subfoveal neovascular AMD
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects who lost fewer than 15 letters in the BCVA score at Month 12 compared to baseline (non-inferiority margin 7%)
pivotal_trials.n: 423 subjects enrolled (143 verteporfin PDT, 140 ranibizumab 0.3mg, 140 ranibizumab 0.5mg)
pivotal_trials.result: At Month 12, loss of <15 letters: 96% LUCENTIS 0.5 mg vs 64% verteporfin PDT (difference 33%, 95% CI 25%, 41%); gain of >=15 letters 40% vs 6% (difference 35%); mean change +11.3 vs -9.5 letters; p<0.01

nct_ctgov.title: A Study to Compare rhuFab V2 With Verteporfin Photodynamic in Treating Subfoveal Neovascular Macular Degeneration

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multi-center, double-blind, double-masked, sham-controlled (superiority) study; subjects received sham, ranibizumab 0.3mg, or ranibizumab 0.5mg injection monthly for 3 doses (Day 0, Month 1, Month 2) and then every 3 months, in a 1:1:1 ratio
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects with or without choroidal neovascularization (CNV) secondary to AMD
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Mean change in BCVA score at Month 12 from baseline
pivotal_trials.result: At Month 12, mean change in BCVA: -0.2 letters LUCENTIS 0.5 mg vs -16.3 letters sham (difference 14.7); loss of <15 letters 90% vs 49% (difference 37%); gain of >=15 letters 13% vs 10%

nct_ctgov.title: A Study of rhuFab V2 (Ranibizumab) in Subjects With Subfoveal Choroidal Neovascularization Secondary to Age-Related Macular Degeneration (AMD)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=6% higher than control) are conjunctival hemorrhage (77% vs 66%), eye pain (37% vs 33%), vitreous floaters (32% vs 10%), increased intraocular pressure (24% vs 7%), and intraocular inflammation (18% vs 11%); serious injection-related events including endophthalmitis occurred in <0.1% of injections; arterial thromboembolic events 2.1% vs 1.1%
target_moa: Ranibizumab is a recombinant humanized antibody Fab fragment that binds to and inhibits the biologic activity of human vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGF-A), active forms of which are targets for therapeutic intervention in neovascular AMD
modality: Antibody fragment (recombinant humanized IgG1 kappa isotype monoclonal antibody fragment / Fab)

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee Meeting was held regarding this application

summary.text: BLA 125156 for Lucentis (ranibizumab injection), a VEGF inhibitor, was a priority (1P) review approved first cycle for treatment of neovascular (wet) AMD, based on three adequate and well-controlled studies (FVF2598g, FVF3192g, and FVF2587g); no advisory committee meeting was held.

citations.quote: The applicant, Genentech Inc. has conducted three adequate and well-controlled studies, FVF2598g, FVF3192g, and FVF2587g which demonstrated statistically and clinically significant differences in the proportion of subjects who lose fewer than 15 letters in best corrected vision at 12 months compared with sham treatment.
Not applicable. No Advisory Committee Meeting will be held regarding this application.
